judgment.rationale: CursorHide can leave the pointer invisible at a UAC boundary; open recovery PR #51547 already modifies the same missing-input and unavailable-position recovery path, but UAC coverage is not yet demonstrated.
evidence: The report uses PowerToys 0.102.3101 and gives the direct sequence: enable CursorHide, then trigger a UAC prompt.
The expected result is a visible pointer during the UAC prompt.
Current AutoHideCursorWorker queues actions from desktop input hooks; AutoHideCursorState restores on mouse input, while SystemCursorHider globally replaces 13 system cursors.

Inspected open PR #51547: timer-sampled movement restoration and a fail-safe restoration when cursor position cannot be read; its source comment explicitly mentions secure desktop. Existing PR evidence does not establish a UAC runtime pass. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/51547
judgment.recommended_action: Compare pointer visibility across the consent prompt with CursorHide disabled, enabled, and with the candidate fix from open PR #51547. Do not assume the candidate covers this case.

reproduce.title: Verify reported CursorHide behavior
prerequisites: Use an isolated disposable Windows VM with default UAC secure-desktop policy; do not lower UAC settings.
steps: Enable CursorHide and hide the pointer by typing.
Launch a trusted Windows administrative task that prompts for UAC consent.
Observe pointer visibility before, during and after the consent prompt; test both accepting and cancelling.
Repeat after idle-triggered hiding and compare with CursorHide disabled.
reproduce.expected_result: The pointer is visible on the consent desktop and is restored safely on return.
